![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14259483/assets/424a2a4b3ed77230d866660fcc8df85e8048eba9f80b3c43dca428d7801e5db7.png)

Given the plots of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ above, find ${h}^{′}(-3)$ where $h(x)=\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}.$
question.worked_solution:
The quotient rule for derivatives gives

$$
{h}^{′}(x)=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)\cdot g(x)-f(x)\cdot {g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(-3)=\frac{{f}^{′}(-3)\cdot g(-3)-f(-3)\cdot {g}^{′}(-3)}{(g(-3))^{2}}.
$$

From the graph above, we obtain that $f(-3)=-1$ and $g(-3)=-2.$

Additionally:

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (-4,0)$ equals $1.$ So, ${f}^{′}(-3)=1.$

- The slope of $g(x)$ on $x\in (-4,4)$ equals $0.$ So, ${g}^{′}(-3)=0.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(-3) & =\frac{{f}^{′}(-3)\cdot g(-3)-f(-3)\cdot {g}^{′}(-3)}{(g(-3))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (-2)-(-1)\cdot 0}{(-2)^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
